key_insight: DFT predicts that GeC/ReS₂ favors direct Z-scheme charge transfer, retaining the redox power needed for photocatalytic overall water splitting.
engineering_relevance: Tensile strain offers a route to tune this candidate hydrogen-production photocatalyst, with predicted solar-to-hydrogen efficiency rising from 41.40% to 60.68% at +6% strain.
method: First-principles DFT analysis of stability and electronic structure.
Band-alignment and Gibbs free-energy comparisons of type-II and direct Z-scheme pathways.
Evaluation of pH-dependent reaction energetics and strain-dependent efficiency.
evidence_signal: Calculations indicate an indirect 1.38 eV band gap, favorable Z-scheme HER energetics across pH 0–14, and light-driven OER across pH 4–14.
watch_item: The efficiencies and dominant charge-transfer mechanism are computational predictions requiring experimental validation, including practical control of +6% tensile strain.
paper_title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
